replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig’s contrast infers personhood from causal structure: timelessly sufficient impersonal conditions would coexist with their effect, whereas libertarian choice could originate a temporal universe without determining conditions. Principal limitation: This comparison neither demonstrates coherent timeless deliberation nor excludes indeterministic, relational, or nonpersonal causal structures capable of producing a first temporal effect. Live burden: Craig must explain how a timeless agent exercises intention and prove the alternatives exhaustive; Flew must answer why an eternally sufficient impersonal cause would not entail an eternal effect. Locked score: The exact 73 reflects logical coherence 68, evidence warrant 59, responsiveness 87, relevance and burden 84, precision and clarity 81, and calibration and charity 62: a responsive, central, clearly reconstructable bridge whose exclusivity and modal mechanism remain substantially underjustified.

Strongest feature: Craig targets Flew’s brute stopping point conditionally: if whatever begins has a cause, the universe cannot be brute, while intuition and uniform experience support that premise. Principal limitation: Observations within a spatiotemporal order do not establish that the principle governs spacetime’s boundary, while calling an uncaused beginning emergence from “nothing” prejudges Flew’s position. Live burden: Craig must justify the domain extension and distinguish nothingness from unexplained initial reality; Flew must identify a principled failure in causal intuition rather than exempting the universe. Locked score: The exact 79 follows from logical coherence 77, evidence warrant 70, responsiveness 88, relevance and burden 85, precision and clarity 85, and calibration and charity 70: a direct, central reply with substantial intuitive warrant, moderated by unresolved cosmic applicability.
